rationale: Both from_bits_unchecked calls are replaced by the checked from_bits_truncate; the to_little_endian side now returns the raw u8 scalar instead of reconstructing the bitflags, so no unsafe reconstruction remains and the serialized bytes are unchanged.
The uninitialized length bump is replaced by Vec::resize, which initializes len zero bytes; the same read buffer length is produced with no unsafe and no uninitialized memory.

The out-of-bounds one-past-the-end pointer from get_unchecked(data.len()) is replaced by integer address arithmetic (as_ptr() as usize + len), so the end pointer is computed without creating an invalid reference/pointer.
evidence_new: let data_ptr_end = data.as_ptr() as usize + data.len();

rationale: The unchecked slice access is replaced by the same integer-address computation, matching the data_ptr_end representation and removing the unsafe get_unchecked.
copy_nonoverlapping on raw pointers is replaced by slice copy_from_slice on exactly the destination range, which copies the same bytes safely and bounds-checks the range.
The unchecked mutable index is replaced by the checked get_mut with an if-let; out-of-range lines are skipped instead of invoking UB, and line_count is a &u64 in the new code so no raw deref remains.
evidence_old: unsafe { *lines.get_unchecked_mut((*line_num - 1) as usize) = line_count as i64; }
evidence_new: if let Some(line) = lines.get_mut((*line_num - 1) as usize) { *line = *line_count as i64; }

rationale: The unsafe Vec::from_raw_parts/forget construction is gone, but the replacement returns a one-element vec and silently drops the len argument, so the shown snippet does not demonstrate that the safe code does the same job. The hunk is clipped; the length-driven construction is missing.

rationale: from_utf8_unchecked is replaced by checked str::from_utf8 with the error mapped into io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, so invalid input yields an error instead of UB and valid input wraps identically.

The untyped unsafe cast_event is eliminated by migrating to the typed event API: wait_for_event returns xcb::Event and the KeyPress variant is destructured by pattern match, giving the same event data with no unsafe.
As in basic_window, the unsafe cast_event is replaced by matching the typed xcb::Event::X(x::Event::KeyPress(key_press)) variant, so the same key press data is obtained safely.

Both ptr::swap calls are replaced by copy-based swaps through ordinary indexing (with an early return for equal indices); no raw-pointer aliasing trick remains, and the safe mem::swap/self.swap equivalent also exists here.
ptr::swap on two element references is replaced by a value swap using the Copy supertrait bound and ordinary indexing; the same elements are exchanged with no unsafe borrow.

mem::uninitialized is replaced by MaybeUninit::uninit, the canonical safe uninitialized-storage API, and from_inline is a safe constructor; the added size/align assert guards custom Array impls and no unsafe remains in the shown code.

The per-extra-element unsafe ptr::copy in the overflow path is removed: the unsafe batch is bounded to lower_size_bound and surplus elements are inserted one-by-one through the safe insert fallback. However the hunk is a fragment of the surrounding unsafe block and raw ptr::offset/ptr::write/ptr::copy on the trailing range still remain, so replacement requires restructuring and unsafe code is retained.

The mem::uninitialized placeholder used with mem::replace/forget is replaced by take_mut::take, a safe take-with-ownership API; the decoder value is moved into a closure and reinstalled, so the uninitialized value and the associated unsafe/forget dance are gone.
Vec::with_capacity plus set_len is replaced by vec![0; BUF_SIZE], which allocates and initializes the same buffer length safely, avoiding handing uninitialized memory to read.
The raw-pointer write through UnsafeCell::with_mut is replaced by a direct field assignment, which stores None in the slot with no unsafe deref and the same effect.

from_unchecked is replaced by masked/select construction using the safe AsciiChar::new plus is_lowercase/is_uppercase helpers, preserving the a-z/A-Z mapping while performing no unchecked construction.

The raw *const T field and unsafe deref (plus unsafe Send/Sync impls) are replaced by storing a projection closure over the guard; Deref now calls (self.projection)(&self.guard), a safe reborrow with no unsafe pointer deref.
Same change as the other arc-swap hunk: the pointer-based MapGuard becomes a closure projection and Deref returns &R safely via the guard, removing the raw deref and unsafe impls.
